summary: The article explains how social media marketing has reshaped local business strategies after September 1, 2023, drawing on quotes from strategists, owners and analysts. It covers algorithm shifts toward community-focused content, micro-influencer partnerships, short-form video, data-driven ad targeting, platform diversity, social responsibility, and omnichannel integration. It concludes that adaptability and sincere community engagement are key to thriving.
one_line: Local businesses are using social media through community content, micro-influencers, short video, data targeting and omnichannel integration, with adaptability as the key to success.
key_facts: Cathy Jenkins, a social media strategist based in Austin, said updates in late 2023 shifted algorithms toward favoring highly engaging, community-focused content.
Algorithms prioritize material that spurs discussions and keeps users on-platform longer, per Cathy Jenkins.
Alan Torres, owner of craft brewery Hop Dreams, recently saw a significant increase in sales thanks to a targeted micro-influencer campaign.
Micro-influencers are personalities with smaller but highly engaged followings, and their followers trust their opinions.
Mia Zhang, a social media manager for several local retail outlets, called short-form videos 'a game-changer' that capture what makes each local business distinct.
TikTok and Instagram's Reels have driven the rise of short-form video as a key marketing format for local businesses.
Derek Simmons, proprietor of the Green Thumb Nursery, uses data on customer preferences, peak engagement times and preferred plant content for hyper-targeted ads.
Tech analyst Brian O'Connell said every new platform is 'a blank canvas' and early adopters can become prominent voices before big brands saturate the space.
Clubhouse offers audio-based networking potential, and AR features are cited as a way to experiment with new platforms.
Maria Gonzales, a café owner in Boulder, gained online support by sharing sustainability initiatives like composting and supporting local farmers.
Digital retail consultant Kevin Patel said 'The future of local business may be omnichannel,' aligning in-store experiences with social media for a cohesive customer journey.
The article concludes that adaptability is crucial: businesses that stay flexible and engage sincerely with their communities are set to thrive.
